title: Voyager
note: Voyager 1 and 2 share one design. Frame (PDS host catalog): HGA boresight -z (dish faces Earth), science boom +y, RTG boom generally -y; the magnetometer boom is on the side opposite the science boom. Values marked 'NASA model' are measured from NASA 3D Resources 'Voyager Probe (B)' where no document gives them.

record_gold.note: linear RGB: mean of mid-brightness pixels (luminance 0.5-0.7) on NASA's cover photo, G/R 0.77 and B/R 0.09, scaled to R 0.85; film colour balance unknown

record_roughness.source: cover_photo, polished finish: mirror-like reflections of the room and hairline scratches
record_roughness.note: glTF roughness, judged by eye against the photo and chosen by the user on the home-page view (earlier 0.35); fully metallic

record_hub.note: eyelet at the centre of NASA's cover photo: ring ~42 px, hole ~20 px radius against the 1072 px rim radius (152 mm); height estimated, not documented

record_roll_deg.note: turns the texture upright (+z) on the +x face; the reference close-up shows the diagrams upright, record and stylus at upper left

scan_platform.note: the NASA model's loose pieces in y > 3.2 (77 pieces: open box faces, rings and discs), grouped into the volumes they bound and read off their bounds: six blanket-wrapped boxes, a vertical post with a tip and a short tube along the boom, two sideways barrels (0.244 and 0.19-0.197 m across) and a dish-shaped telescope 0.485 m across facing +x with a 0.18 m secondary on a stalk. Two gaps under 1 cm closed so the pieces touch (lower box top raised to the body box, telescope back moved to the lower box's side). Which instrument each piece is (ISS cameras, IRIS, UVS, PPS per kohlhase1977's list) is not stated in any opened source, so the names describe shapes. The two barrels are open sunshades with a lens at the back (NASA's are open tubes); the telescope is a bowl 0.485 m across and 0.155 m deep (its ring spans x 0.145-0.30) opening toward +x, its secondary on a 0.055 m stalk. scan_lower is a half cylinder hanging under the platform, not a box (a box sized to its bounds took its texture flat, showing a half disc on the box's side): radius 0.2745 (y 3.612-4.161 about 3.887, 0.274 deep), flat top, x -0.289 to 0.139, its -x end tapering to x -0.351 where the section is 0.132 wide and 0.094 deep (built round, radius 0.132). Top at z -0.124 (the body box's base) rather than NASA's -0.132, as before.

bus_details.note: NASA model (nasa_3d_voyager), measured from its loose pieces (each strut is several flat faces, merged; endpoints are the ends along the principal axis). top_blanket: the domed thermal blanket on the bus top, [r, z] from the outer envelope of its 672-vertex piece in 5 cm radius bands (mid z of each band; the blanket is draped, so z varies by up to 4 cm at one radius); it replaces a 0.35 m post that stood in for it. bottom_plate: the decagonal plate under the bus, corners 0.97-0.98 m out at z -0.238, same turn as the bus; its top is set on our bus bottom. under_legs: eight legs from four bus corners to eight feet at z -1.041 (the reference has no adapter ring; it replaces four estimated struts and a ring). Leg radius from the spread of each leg's faces (about 25 mm across). under_panel: a flat panel under the bus on the +y side, frame edges as given, two faces 15 mm apart; carried by two struts from near the +y feet. record_boxes: a small box under the golden record and one opposite it, bounds of their faces. top_boxes: two units on the bus top at -x/-y, each a grille housing overhanging the bus edge and a body box behind it, measured in axes along top_boxes_axis (the body's top slopes from z 0.384 to 0.442 in the reference; built flat). ring_struts: two V pairs from the bus top to the upper ring's base on the +-x sides. Struts from the bus to the science and magnetometer boom roots are left for the boom pass.

open_questions: Surface finishes (gold/black blankets, bare metal): no document; photos needed.
Whip directions relative to the booms: PRA paper Fig. 5 text unreadable; needs a visual check.
RTG boom geometry, HGA depth, magnetometer boom angle and support truss: only from the NASA model.
MHW-RTG fin span: only from the NASA model (0.63 m).

Golden record cover: what the Smithsonian's 1.3 cm depth includes, engraving depth and method, hub height, and the exact turn on the bus are not documented; the gold finish method is not given by NASA.
Scan platform: which piece is which instrument (ISS narrow/wide cameras, IRIS, UVS, PPS); layout and sizes now from the NASA model.

Bus details: what the boxes under the golden record and the two grille units on the bus top are (geometry from the NASA model). The panel under the bus is the optical calibration target and radiator (facts.under_panel_identity).

Thrusters: positions, cluster layout and pointing of the 16 hydrazine thrusters are not in any opened source (facts.thrusters); NTRS 19810059702 and 19820062089 (AACS papers) may have them but list no PDF.

bake.note: Base colour projected from NASA's 3D model (nasa_3d_voyager: one 1024 px photo-textured atlas, about 7.5 mm/px on the dish and 10 mm/px on the bus, so a 2048 px atlas holds all its detail). Two passes like Perseverance's: a near one, then a far one for stand-in faces the near pass misses. '_root' (a 24-vertex box with no material) is left out. No normal map: NASA's geometry adds little and the budget is 1.5 MB.
